title: String Suffix Structures: Suffix Array, Suffix Automaton, Aho–Corasick
relevance: Medium — almost never a literal OA template (Striver skips these), but multi-pattern dictionary search, distinct/repeated substrings, and “k-th substring” show up in harder screens; primarily Candidate Master rating-builders.
company_notes: Longest duplicated/repeated substring (appears ≥ twice) → max LCP or binary search + hash (LC-style Hard). Dictionary/multi-needle “which keywords appear in the document” → Aho–Corasick (or SA if one fixed text, many queries). Distinct or k-th lex substring → SA+LCP or SAM path DP (CSES Order I/II / CF 128B). Harder CP: cyclic minimal rotation, “string must contain pattern P”, lex-smallest erase/append builds (CSES Required Substring / CF Erase and Extend).

phases.goal: Map wording to suffix array+LCP, suffix automaton, or Aho–Corasick instead of O(n^2) substring scans.

must_hit.point: Signals: “many patterns vs one text”, “count distinct / k-th / repeating substrings”, “substring that appears in ≥2 places”, or “build string avoiding / forcing a pattern” → suffix structures (SA/SAM/AC), not naive scans.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Lists those signal phrases and reaches for SA/SAM/AC rather than O(n^2) enumeration.

must_hit.point: “Longest substring that appears ≥ twice” / longest duplicated substring → max LCP (or binary search + hash).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names the ≥2-occurrence longest-repeat shape and answers max LCP (optionally BS+hash).

must_hit.point: “Find which of these keywords appear in the document” → Aho–Corasick (or SA if one fixed text and many queries).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Maps multi-needle dictionary search to AC, mentioning SA as the fixed-text alternative.

must_hit.point: Tool pick cue: one pattern → KMP/Z/hash; many patterns → AC; all-substring aggregates / k-th / LCS of two strings → SA+LCP or SAM.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States that one-vs-many vs all-substring/k-th/two-string-LCS split across KMP/Z/hash, AC, and SA/SAM.

probes: What wording makes you reach for SA+LCP, SAM, or Aho–Corasick instead of hashing/KMP alone?
Is this one pattern, many patterns, or an all-substring / k-th / repeat aggregate?

hints.1: Listen for multi-pattern vs one text, distinct/k-th/repeating substrings, or ≥2 occurrences.
hints.2: One pattern → KMP/Z/hash; many needles → AC; distinct/k-th/repeat/LCS-of-two → SA+LCP or SAM.
hints.3: Say: many patterns vs one text / distinct / k-th / repeating / appears in ≥2 places / avoid-or-force a pattern → SA, SAM, or AC; longest ≥2-occurrence → max LCP; keyword dictionary in a document → AC (or SA on fixed text).

phases.goal: State how SA+LCP, SAM, and AC index substrings so queries become binary searches or automaton walks.

must_hit.point: Suffix array = sorted list of suffix starts; pair with Kasai LCP for adjacent overlaps — distinct count = n(n+1)/2 − ∑LCP, longest repeat = max LCP, pattern search = binary search on SA.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Defines SA+LCP roles and states the distinct, max-repeat, and binsearch-on-SA uses.

must_hit.point: Suffix automaton = minimal DFA of all substrings (O(n) states); len[v] − len[link[v]] = new distinct substrings ending in state v; endpos / link-tree DP for occurrences.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Calls SAM a minimal all-substring DFA with O(n) states and states the len−link distinct and endpos/link-tree occurrence plan.

must_hit.point: Aho–Corasick = trie of many patterns + KMP-style fail links — scan the text once and aggregate matches on the fail tree.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes trie + fail links, one text scan, and fail-tree aggregation.

must_hit.point: Minimal cyclic rotation: SA on s+s or Booth’s O(n); contain/avoid pattern: automaton DP on KMP/AC/SAM states with accepted/forbidden marks.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names SA-of-s+s or Booth for least rotation, and state DP for contain/avoid.

probes: How do SA+LCP, SAM, and AC each turn substring queries into searches or walks?
For distinct count vs multi-pattern match vs minimal rotation, which structure and why?

hints.1: Index all substrings (or the dictionary) so you never rescan O(n^2) pairs.
hints.2: SA sorts suffix starts + LCP; SAM is the minimal substring DFA; AC is a multi-pattern trie with fail links.
hints.3: Say: SA+LCP → distinct = n(n+1)/2−∑LCP, longest repeat = max LCP, pattern via SA binsearch; SAM → O(n) states, distinct via len−link, occurrences via endpos/link tree; AC → trie+fail, one scan, aggregate on fail tree; rotation via SA(s+s) or Booth O(n).

phases.goal: Build SA+Kasai, SAM extend with endpos/link DP, and AC fail/go correctly enough to solve core shapes.

must_hit.point: Build SA in O(n log n) (doubling + radix) or call ACL suffix_array; always build Kasai LCP in O(n) next.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States O(n log n) SA (doubling/radix or ACL) then Kasai LCP in O(n).

must_hit.point: SAM node fields: next[], link, len (+ firstpos / endpos size); online sam_extend(c); distinct = ∑(len[v]−len[link[v]]); propagate endpos sizes up the link tree (larger len → smaller); clone nodes start at 0.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Lists those fields, extend, distinct sum, upward endpos push, and clone endpos 0.

must_hit.point: Aho–Corasick: insert patterns into a trie, BFS fail links (fail = KMP on the trie), go(v,c) transitions; exit/output links for matches; for counts ++cnt[state] while scanning, then sum cnt over fail-tree subtrees (or push to parent).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes trie insert, BFS fails, go, output links, and fail-tree count push/sum.

must_hit.point: Pattern in text via SA: binary-search first/last suffix with that prefix (O(|P| log n) compares); k-th distinct: walk SA/SAM counting new prefixes per state; multiplicity variants use SAM endpos sizes × path DP.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States SA prefix range binsearch cost and SA/SAM walks for k-th distinct vs multiplicity.

probes: Walk through building SA+LCP, then how you’d count distinct substrings or search a pattern.
How do you construct SAM or AC and get occurrence/match counts?

hints.1: Separate construction (SA/Kasai, sam_extend, AC BFS fails) from the aggregation query.
hints.2: After SA always Kasai; SAM needs endpos up the link tree with clones at 0; AC marks then pushes on the fail tree.
hints.3: Say: SA O(n log n)+Kasai O(n); distinct n(n+1)/2−∑LCP; SA pattern binsearch O(|P| log n); SAM next/link/len/extend, distinct ∑(len−len[link]), endpos up link tree, clones 0; AC trie+BFS fail+go, ++cnt then fail-tree sums.

phases.goal: State the construction and query costs that appear for SA, LCP, SAM, and SA pattern search.

must_hit.point: SA via doubling + radix (or ACL) is O(n log n); Kasai LCP is O(n).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Quotes O(n log n) for SA and O(n) for Kasai LCP.

must_hit.point: SAM has O(n) states; indexing avoids O(n^2) substring scans.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States O(n) SAM states and contrasts with O(n^2) scans.

must_hit.point: Binary-searching a pattern as a SA prefix costs O(|P| log n) compares.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Gives the O(|P| log n) SA pattern-search bound.

must_hit.point: Minimal rotation can be Booth’s O(n) (or SA on s+s); large-n erase/append (Erase and Extend Hard) forces linear / O(n log n) SA or dueling, not O(n^2).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions Booth O(n) and that hard erase/extend needs linear or O(n log n), not O(n^2).

probes: What are the build costs for SA, Kasai LCP, and SAM, and the SA pattern-search cost?
When does an O(n^2) string build fail the constraints here?

hints.1: Separate SA build, LCP build, SAM size, and pattern binsearch costs.
hints.2: SA O(n log n), Kasai O(n), SAM O(n) states, SA pattern O(|P| log n); hard builds forbid O(n^2).
hints.3: Say: SA O(n log n)+Kasai O(n); SAM O(n) states vs O(n^2) scans; pattern on SA O(|P| log n); Booth O(n) for minimal rotation; Erase and Extend Hard needs linear/O(n log n), not O(n^2).

phases.goal: Catch wrong LCP/endpos/fail-tree bookkeeping and picking the wrong string tool.

must_hit.point: Forgetting Kasai LCP after building SA, or mis-stating distinct as something other than n(n+1)/2 − ∑LCP[i] (and longest repeating length as max LCP).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Insists on building Kasai next and using those exact distinct / max-LCP formulas.

must_hit.point: On SAM, failing to propagate endpos sizes up the link tree, or initializing clone nodes with nonzero endpos instead of 0.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Requires upward endpos push and clone nodes starting at 0.

must_hit.point: On AC multi-pattern counts, only incrementing cnt[state] while scanning and never summing/pushing over the fail-tree subtrees (or to parent).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Requires the fail-tree aggregation step after the scan increments.

must_hit.point: Using one-pattern KMP/Z/hash when many patterns need AC, or using AC when the ask is all-substring aggregates / k-th / LCS of two strings (need SA+LCP or SAM).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Restates the pick-tool split and flags the wrong-structure choice.

probes: What breaks distinct-count or occurrence answers if LCP, endpos, or AC fail-tree bookkeeping is wrong?
When is AC the wrong tool versus SA/SAM?

hints.1: Check LCP after SA, SAM clones/endpos direction, and AC fail-tree push.
hints.2: Distinct needs ∑LCP; SAM clones start at 0 and push endpos up; AC must aggregate on the fail tree; match tool to one vs many vs all-substring.
hints.3: Say: always Kasai after SA; distinct = n(n+1)/2−∑LCP, longest repeat = max LCP; SAM endpos up link tree, clones 0; AC ++cnt then fail-tree sum/push; one pattern→KMP/Z/hash, many→AC, all-substring/k-th/two-string LCS→SA+LCP or SAM.

tradeoffs.strong_answer: One pattern → KMP/Z/hash; many patterns against one text → Aho–Corasick (trie + fail links, one scan). Prefer SA when the text is fixed and queries are many SA prefix searches.

tradeoffs.topic: SA+LCP vs SAM for distinct / k-th / repeats
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Both handle distinct substrings and k-th walks; SA+LCP gives distinct via n(n+1)/2−∑LCP and longest repeat via max LCP; SAM gives distinct via ∑(len[v]−len[link[v]]) and occurrence/multiplicity via endpos and link-tree / path DP.

tradeoffs.topic: SA binary search vs Aho–Corasick for multi-pattern existence
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Finding Patterns-style checks can use SA range binary search or an Aho walk; AC is the natural multi-needle scan-and-aggregate tool, while SA shines for prefix/occurrence queries on one prepared text.

tradeoffs.topic: Booth vs SA of s+s for minimal rotation
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Least cyclic shift via Booth’s O(n) or by building SA on s+s; both are valid—Booth is linear dedicated, SA reuses the general suffix template.

gotchas.trap: Building a suffix array and skipping Kasai LCP.
gotchas.correction: Always build Kasai LCP in O(n) next; distinct substrings use n(n+1)/2 − ∑LCP[i], and longest repeating substring length is max LCP.

gotchas.trap: Initializing SAM clone nodes with the same endpos size as the original instead of 0.
gotchas.correction: Clone nodes start at 0; propagate endpos sizes up the SAM link tree (larger len → smaller).

gotchas.trap: Counting AC matches only at the states visited while scanning the text.
gotchas.correction: After ++cnt[state] on the scan, sum cnt over fail-tree subtrees (or push to parent) so matches implied by fail links are counted.

gotchas.trap: Reaching for AC when the problem needs all-substring aggregates, k-th substring, or LCS-of-two-strings style answers.
gotchas.correction: Pick SA+LCP or SAM for those; reserve AC for many patterns vs one text (and automaton DP for contain/avoid).

gotchas.trap: Solving large-n erase/append lex-smallest builds with an O(n^2) approach.
gotchas.correction: Hard Erase and Extend forces linear / O(n log n) SA or dueling, not O(n^2).
